scope: Environment-level lightweight training and guarded batch harness for agentic demo-video data production
summary: Implemented and CPU-validated a reusable demo-video factory protocol with immutable command workers, baseline-bound diagnostics, hard quality and human gates, capability non-regression, physical-GPU selection and leasing, complete-recipe exploration, leave-one-group-out ridge routing, promotion gates, accepted-video indexing, and planner-distillation preference export. The environment capability exists, but no real multi-scene GPU tournament or fresh production-cost acceptance run has completed.
lessons: Successful agentic traces become reusable only after generator, evaluator, recipe, cost, artifact, and split semantics share one versioned episode contract.
Production early stopping creates biased routing data; bootstrap and periodic exploration must measure every recipe in every held group.
Aggregate utility cannot substitute for per-capability non-regression or explicit human vetoes.
A small router can be promoted independently of heavy video models while retaining a preference export for later planner distillation.
limitations: All new acceptance evidence is CPU-only and uses synthetic command-adapter videos rather than real generator outputs.
No new foundation-model, video LoRA, planner LoRA, SFT, or preference checkpoint was trained.
No real held-scene campaign has measured acceptance-rate or GPU-cost improvement.
The reference contract and worker protocol still need domain-specific adapters for the selected real video pipeline.
next_actions: Wrap the strongest accepted AC-WM or H3/Wan demo path and its evaluator as factory worker recipes.
Run complete tournaments on at least two independent licensed real-scene groups and append every outcome.
Train and promote the first real-input router, then evaluate it on a fresh held scene with acceptance and cost gates.
Only after real router promotion, test a small planner-distillation adapter against the same frozen groups.
